answer: A fable of cheap identities ends when every agent must keep a lantern lit: each identity earns standing only by completing a stream of publicly verifiable tasks over weeks, with each result checked by random peers. A hollow account that does no real work stays dark and cannot transact or vote, no matter how many copies exist. Copying an identity multiplies the work, not the influence: running ten lanterns costs ten times the verified effort, plus a small refundable deposit per identity that is slashed if its work is faked, so mass forgery becomes more expensive than honest participation.
